newsitem.title: INDONESIA: OPINION-1996 results reinforce bullish market view.
newsitem.headline: OPINION-1996 results reinforce bullish market view.

text.p: By Felix Otto D'Souza, head of research,
Peregrine Sewu Securities, Jakarta
JAKARTA, May 1 - As we approach the end of the full year 1996 reporting season, market earnings growth looks likely to come in slightly above Peregrine's forecast and ahead of market consensus.
As of April 30, 90 percent of all listed companies had reported their 1996 results and the aggregate increase in net profit from the previous year was 23.5 percent.
The aggregate profit for the companies included in Peregrine's universe of stocks covered exceeded Peregrine forecasts by 2.1 percent.
With selected unaudited results first starting to trickle out some two months ago, the healthy reporting season has already begun to be reflected in analysts' 1997 earnings forecasts.
Although Peregrine's estimate for 1997 market earnings growth remains at around 19 percent, consensus forecasts have been revised up to a similar level from below 17 percent in January this year.
Such earnings upgrades certainly buck the regional trend and should attract the interest of momentum investors and general funds that are not Indonesian specific.
GUDANG CARAM LEADS THE WAY
Amongst the large blue chips, a strong performance came from Gudang Garam in the cigarette sector (net profit up 79 percent y-y and nine percent ahead of Peregrine's forecast).

Banks performed well, although slightly worse than Peregrine estimates with strong results from Bank Danamon (net profit up 52 percent y-y, one percent below Peregrine's forecast), BDNI (up 36 percent, 12 percent above), BII (up 35 percent, five percent below), Bank Bira (up 98 percent, three percent below) and Lippo Bank (up 39 percent, four percent below).

Selected property stocks showed solid growth such as Mulialand (net profit up 34 percent, three percent above Peregrine's forecast), K.I. Jababeka (up 36 percent, three percent above) and JIHD (up 86 percent, nine percent above).
Low-end retailer Ramayana also put in a good performance with 1996 net profit up 91 percent, three percent above Peregrine's estimate.
Cigarette stocks, banks and selected property plays will continue to show strong earnings growth in 1997 and remain amongst Peregrine's top stock picks.
We expect all the companies mentioned above to continue to be market outperformers over the next 12 months.
Transport play Steady Safe also looks very cheap at current levels in the light of almost 40 percent compound earnings growth through the rest of the decade (after 36 percent in 1996).
Toll road play, CMNP, showed 1996 earnings growth of 31 percent, in line with Peregrine's estimates and also features on Peregrine's buy list.
SMALL CAP WONDERS
Some small cap stocks put in startling performances, although they had little impact on overall market earnings growth.

Amongst those companies with reasonable liquidity and good prospects for 1997 Peregrine highlights cocoa grinder and speciality fat producer Cahaya Kalbar (net profit up 392 percent y-y). The stock trades on a 1997 P/E of just 11x with a four-year CAGR of 30 percent.
Also on 11x 1997 earnings is Davomas Abadi, another cocoa grinder looking at compound earnings growth of 25 percent through 2000. Davomas reported earnings growth of 84 percent in 1996.

Duty free retailer Sona Topas also looks good value at below 13x 1997 earnings. Earnings in 1996 only grew 16 percent for this very high margin retailer but a major store expansion in Bali should provide compound earnings growth of around 40 percent over the next four years.
TELKOM GROWTH SET TO SLOW
Telkom posted annual growth in net earnings of an apparently impressive 66 percent. However, the earnings growth is a result of the restructuring in 1995/96 and IPO proceeds.
This was 15 percent ahead of Peregrine's forecast on the back of better-than-expected reductions in operating expenses following the restructuring.
However, Peregrine is calling for earnings growth of less than five percent in 1997 as sharply reduced revenues from lost interconnection fees hit the bottom line.
ECONOMIC FUNDAMENTALS STILL POSITIVE

Bank Indonesia's eclectic approach to economic management has resulted in stability and market confidence. The current BI governor, Soadradjad Djiwandono, strongly believes in avoiding shocks to the market.
Under his leadership, central bank policy in the last two years has been characterised by a series of minor measures introduced with plenty of lead time.
BI officials indicate that the bank's style is unlikely to change and any steps taken to cool down the persistently high M2 growth will be carefully considered and introduced gradually.
Despite the strong M2 growth, inflation remains under control. GDP growth is holding up well and the curent account deficit is well below four percent of GDP.

Peregrine currently expects headline inflation to fall to 6.7 percent in 1997 from 7.9 percent in 1996, and 1997 GDP growth to come in at 7.3 percent, only slightly below the strong 7.8 percent for 1996.
NOT ANOTHER THAILAND
With jitters continuing to be felt around the region following financial meltdown in Thailand and South Korea, Indonesia's banking and property sectors are naturally coming under close scrutiny.
The absence of any recent speculative bubble or of any major fall in property prices is re-assuring. Whilst GDP growth remains firm, there is little to worry about.

Support for continued stable economic growth comes from a relatively strong export performance compared to regional peers and strong investment spending on infrastructure and export-related industries.
A fairly stable real effective exchange rate (in a falling inflation environment) and a large component of commodity related exports reduce the downside potential for year-to-year changes in exports.

Peregrine continues to believe that politics should not be a major factor in dictating investments. With the campaign period well under way, there have been no significant disturbances and meetings have been good-natured.
Although the market should continue to see generally thin volume and little direction until the end of May, we are confident of a strong performance following the elections on May 29.
Peregrine is still looking for the market to end the year between 750 and 800 based on strong corporate earnings growth and solid economic fundamentals.
(NOTE-The view expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as reflecting the views of Reuters).
